target_customer: Game developers and robotics teams that want fast learned world simulators instead of hand coded engines
problem: Hard coded game and physics engines are expensive to build, and existing neural world models are too slow and compute hungry to run interactively on consumer hardware.
business_model: Not yet clear. Model licensing and fine tuned simulators for gaming and robotics partners were the stated targets.

founders.name: Rami Seid
previous_startups: Cofounded a telecommunications company (outcome not stated)
founders.background_notes: First job was an ML engineer internship at a robotics lab, later CTO of a govtech contractor.

founders.name: Alberto Hojel
education: UC Berkeley, computer science (third party profile)
founders.background_notes: A third party profile describes him as a Berkeley AI Research ML researcher. The YC page gives only the first name Alberto.

competitors.name: Decart (Oasis)
competitors.what: Real time playable Minecraft style world model released with Etched
competitors.traction_then: Public demo at 20 FPS at 360 by 360 on an H100, open weights, press coverage in October 2024
competitors.funding_then: $21M from Sequoia and Oren Zeev at launch, then a $32M round in December 2024

competitors.name: Google DeepMind Genie 2
competitors.what: Generates interactive 3D worlds from an image

technical_complexity.rationale: Training an action conditioned diffusion world model with 128x tokenizer compression that runs at 20 FPS on one consumer GPU is research grade work for a team of three, with open problems in long term consistency.

defensibility.rationale: The speed advantage came from a tokenizer insight that can be published or reimplemented, and larger labs have far more compute. Little data or switching cost lock in was shown.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Well funded rivals (Decart raised $300M later per press) and big labs moved into world models. Cofounder Alberto Hojel joined Roblox in late 2025 to build a game cartridge harness, a talent absorption but not a reported acquisition.

market_need_then: Interest in world models for games and robot training was rising in late 2024, driven by Oasis and Genie 2. Evidence of paying demand for Lucid itself was not found.

branding.domain_note: Uses lucid.ai, a short exact match domain. YC contact email uses lucidsim.co. How the domain was acquired was not found.

identity.logo: Not described in any source found
identity.voice_and_tone: Poetic, for example every mind contains infinite worlds waiting to unfold and are you lucid

branding.brand_signature: Dream and lucid dreaming theme tying the name to simulated worlds
branding.community_and_virality: Founder substack and Hugging Face posts on Lucid v1 reached ML hobbyists, and a Jan 2026 HUGE Magazine feature covered it. No merch found.

brand_strength.rationale: The name fits the product concept and the domain is strong, but Lucid is very common as a company name (Lucid Motors and others) and press about the brand itself is minimal.

outcome_analysis: Lucid built a technically notable fast Minecraft world model in 2024 and joined YC in Winter 2025 with three people. No funding or exit has been found, and a Roblox post of June 2026 says cofounder Alberto Hojel joined Roblox in late 2025, so the company's current activity and the founder split are unclear. The story is still open, with strong competition from better funded world model labs.
notes: No funding information found beyond YC (Altss lists family office investors behind a paywall). The Roblox article describes Hojel as having started Lucid AI and joined Roblox in late 2025 but gives no deal terms and does not say whether Lucid continues, so exit stays none while the directory says Active. A third party profile of Hojel's Berkeley background is unverified. Competitors Decart and Genie 2 are dated to around the batch.
